stem.text: Spea multiplicata is one of several species of American spadefoot toad.
Young spadefoot toads are called tadpoles and live in water in ponds.
S. multiplicata tadpoles show three different phenotypes due to genetic variation. The three phenotypes are: detritus feeder, intermediate and carnivore.
Detritus feeders are small, and carnivores are large. Intermediates vary in size between the two extremes.
A detritus feeder and a carnivore are shown in Fig. 7.1.

stem.alt: Carnivorous and detritus-feeding Spea multiplicata tadpoles, with a fairy shrimp labelled.

stem.text: Scientists counted the number of each type of tadpole in two different ponds: pond 1 and pond 2.

stem.text: Describe and suggest explanations for the type of natural selection that appears to be acting in pond 1.

explanation.text: When food is scarce, each specialised extreme can exploit a different food resource. Poorly competing intermediates are selected against, producing disruptive selection.

reasoningChain: Link the loss of intermediates to competition for scarce food.

inferredMistakes.text: Calling selection for both extremes directional selection.

explanation.text: With abundant food, intermediates can use a wider range of resources without the same competitive disadvantage. Selection favouring the intermediate phenotype and acting against extremes is stabilising.

Use food availability and dietary range to explain its advantage.

stem.text: A student suggested that the variation in S. multiplicata tadpoles could lead to sympatric speciation in some populations.
Outline the features of sympatric speciation.

points.text: new species form due to reproductive isolation ;
caused by, ecological / behavioural, separation / isolation / differences ;
in same geographical region ;
AVP ;

explanation.text: Sympatric speciation involves reproductive isolation within the same geographical region. Ecological or behavioural differences can reduce interbreeding without a physical barrier separating the populations.

reasoningChain: State that populations remain in the same geographical area.
Identify how reproductive isolation can develop within it.

inferredMistakes.text: Using geographical separation as the defining feature of sympatric speciation.
